notes: Swarm's budget checks (M4). Written by the Technical Director at stage 0, before the game exists: until tests/games/swarm/main.asm does, the runner reports SKIP. That file is the gameplay-engineer's, two lines: '#define AUTOPLAY' then '#import "games/swarm/src/main.asm"'. AUTOPLAY makes the game play the designer's worst case by itself (wave 12, scripted stick, nothing dies): docs/games/swarm/memory-map.md#labels-the-game-must-provide lists what it does and every label these checks read. 'stage' is the M4 stage the game's code has reached (docs/milestones/M4-training-game.md, stages 1-5): the gameplay-engineer sets it at the start of each stage and changes nothing else here. Checks with a higher from_stage print PENDING. Units: raster cycles, DMA included, IRQs excluded for main-loop routines (engine/README.md#budget-units). Every game limit is an estimate until its stage measures it; a failing check is reported with the measured figure, and the Technical Director re-baselines. The per-routine limits add up to 6,075 for game_update (input measured at 40; collisions 2,825 since stage 2, when the collision module was measured; and since the stage 3 budget decisions of 2026-10-02: player_update 290, a short routine in the display with a fixed badline and sprite allowance instead of x 1.27, pshot_update and stars_update 60 each, measured border routines), + 500 for the sound tick = 6,575 against the engine's 7,200: 625 of headroom, which the idle check enforces (it was 585, and 935 before stage 2). STAGE 1 FIGURES CARRY NO DMA: with 3 sprites, game_update runs on raster lines 23-31, above the first badline (measured, docs/games/swarm/memory-map.md#stage-1-measured), so the display allowance (x 1.27) in every limit is untested until stage 2 puts the formation on screen. For that reason no limit here is re-baselined to a stage 1 measurement; each source line records the stage 1 figure beside the estimate. STAGE 2 PART A (formation, no collisions) was measured by tests/games/swarm/stage2a_costs.py, results beside it: still all above the first badline (docs/games/swarm/memory-map.md#stage-2-part-a-measured). STAGE 2 PART B (hits, explosions, score) was measured by tests/games/swarm/stage2b_costs.py, results beside it (docs/games/swarm/memory-map.md#stage-2-part-b-measured). SAMPLE COUNTS: a routine in the top border has a cost that depends only on its own state, so its count covers that state's cycle (stars 48 frames: 300; formation 192: 600); a routine in the display (player_update, collide_update, diver_update, game_update) lands on a different raster line every frame and the AUTOPLAY script repeats only after thousands of frames, so 600 samples are a look, not a proof: its limit is the counted worst case and make test-long is the longer look. WHAT AUTOPLAY CAN'T MEASURE (nothing dies in it) is measured on the game build with states set through the monitor, by a stageN_costs.py beside this file: docs/games/swarm/memory-map.md#what-autoplay-cannot-measure. A stage built in parts: memory-map.md#labels-the-game-must-provide, last paragraphs. warmup_frames 400: boot, the wave intro (100 frames) and the first launches; the game's own GAME_IDLE_WARMUP is 200 frames. The first memory check runs 3,000 more frames and the others read at that same moment (after_frames 0), except the stage 5 soak.

checks.name: game_update: all game logic in the main loop
checks.source: docs/games/swarm/memory-map.md#frame-budget, row 'Main loop, game_update in all': the sum of the rows, an estimate until stage 3 measures the full mix. 6,075 since the stage 3 budget decisions (2026-10-02): row 3 raised to 290, rows 4 and 10 lowered to 60 (it was 6,115 from stage 2's collision figure, 5,765 before). Raster cycles, IRQs excluded. Stage 1 measured: max 580 in this AUTOPLAY build, lines 23-31, no DMA. Stage 2 part A: 841-1,007, lines 23-39. Stage 2 part B: 883-2,217, ending on lines 37-58 (tests/games/swarm/stage2b_costs.txt)

checks.name: player_update
checks.source: docs/games/swarm/memory-map.md#frame-budget, row 3, and #short-routines-in-the-display. The only short routine that runs after the collisions, in the display, so its allowance is fixed, not x 1.27: 150 CPU (122 measured moving and firing + 28 counted for stage 3's respawn flash) + a badline (43) + the fetches of 8 sprites on each of the 5 lines it can touch (95) = 288 (tests/games/swarm/short_routine_dma.py), rounded to 290. It was 200. Raster cycles, IRQs excluded. Measured so far: max 122-123 (stage 1 and stage 2 part B: no firing pass has met a badline yet). 600 samples: the worst pass needs a firing frame (1 in 10) to start within about 3 lines before a badline (3 lines in 8) inside an enemy row; a sampled maximum of a display routine is still not its worst case (the AUTOPLAY script repeats only after thousands of frames), so the limit is the counted worst and make test-long is the longer look

checks.name: pshot_update (2 player shots)
checks.source: docs/games/swarm/memory-map.md#frame-budget, row 4. Measured 43 (stage 1 and every run since), always in the top border (it runs before the formation, by line 31): no badline, and the only sprite DMA that can reach it is a wrapped diver's from stage 3 (3 sprites: 52 by count, tests/games/swarm/short_routine_dma.txt). 43 + 5% + that = 60. It was 150, an estimate with a display allowance it doesn't need. Raster cycles, IRQs excluded. Its cost has no long cycle (2 shots, each moved or skipped), so 300 samples see every case

checks.name: panel_update
checks.source: docs/games/swarm/memory-map.md#frame-budget, row 9. Estimate (CPU cycles counted from the intended code x 1.27 for DMA); raster cycles, IRQs excluded. Replace with max over the run + ~5% once measured (Technical Director). The limit is per frame of play: score, lives and wave dirty, which AUTOPLAY sets every frame. Stage 1 measured: 231 for those three, 9 with nothing dirty, no DMA. The four-field redraw with the high score (about 325, counted) happens only in panel_init and on entering game over, is exempt and is not measured here; from stage 2 panel_update is called straight after input_read so that it stays in the top border (docs/games/swarm/memory-map.md#the-panels-budget)

checks.name: stars_update
checks.source: docs/games/swarm/memory-map.md#frame-budget, row 10, and #order-of-the-frame. Measured 56-57 in the top border (stages 1 and 2 part A), + 5% = 60. It was 100. DECIDED 2026-10-02: stars_update is called straight after panel_update (lines 27-29: no badline, and no sprite DMA before line 30), where its cost depends on nothing but its own star counter, which repeats every 48 frames: 300 samples are 6 whole turns, so the maximum seen is the maximum. UNTIL THE GAMEPLAY-ENGINEER MOVES THE CALL THIS CHECK FAILS, as intended: called after the collisions (the stage 2 part B build, commit 2dee8cf) it meets badlines and measures 100 over 300 passes and 129 over 600 (tests/games/swarm/stage2b_costs.txt); by count up to 157 (tests/games/swarm/short_routine_dma.txt). Raster cycles, IRQs excluded

checks.name: formation_update (18 enemies)
checks.source: docs/games/swarm/memory-map.md#frame-budget, row 5, and #row-5-the-formation-and-its-explosions. 750, unchanged: 437 measured (drift turn and animation swap in one frame) + 190 counted for 4 explosion slots (3 ending at 53, 1 animating at 31) = 627 CPU, + up to 3 wrapped divers' sprite DMA above line 51 (735 by count, tests/games/swarm/short_routine_dma.txt). The wind-up wobble is NOT here: it is diver_update's (row 6). Raster cycles, IRQs excluded. Measured: stage 2 part A 323-437; part B 352-466 in this AUTOPLAY build (4 free slots) and 431-538 in the game with 4 slots animating then ending together (tests/games/swarm/stage2b_costs.txt), on lines 24-37, no DMA. AUTOPLAY can't measure the explosions (nothing dies): that figure comes from the game build with states set through the monitor. 600 samples: the drift's whole period at loop 3 is 192 frames and the swap's 32, so 600 passes see the turn and the swap together (300 saw 437 in part A; 600 is three whole drift periods)

checks.name: collide_update (42 box tests and their responses)
checks.source: docs/games/swarm/memory-map.md#frame-budget, row 8 and #the-collision-budget (Technical Director, 2026-10-02). 2,825 = 2,450 for the 42 tests (measured in tests/engine/collision: 1,813 with no DMA, max 2,335 through the display on lines 39-89, + 5%) + 375 for the responses to 2 enemy hits or a player hit (estimate, 295 CPU x 1.27). It was 2,475 on a count of 1,641 for the tests. Still an estimate for the game: its caller, its responses and where it lands in the frame are unmeasured. FALLBACK TRIGGER (the gameplay-engineer switches parked enemies to the row/column lookup and reports): this check's max over 2,050 in stage 2 part B (no divers or enemy shots yet), or over 2,825 from stage 3. Stage 2 part B measured: 18-1,192 in this AUTOPLAY build on lines 34-55 (almost no DMA), 1,245 in the game for two hits in one frame (tests/games/swarm/stage2b_costs.txt). Stage 3 expectation (counted): 1,245 + 571 for the player's two scans and 3 divers in a shot's band = 1,816 CPU, x 1.35 through the display = about 2,450; about 2,600 with a player hit answered in the same frame
